**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

**What I checked**
- §§1.1–1.3 (p0005–p0007): HDI designs, develops, hosts and bears all cost of the Site.
- §2.1 (p0016): we supply all Content; §2.2/§7.1: customer orders and customer e-mail lists flow through the Site.
- §5.2 (p0032): we have artistic/editorial control and approval rights — control, but not title.
- §6.1 (p0038–p0039): only a limited, non-exclusive licence of our "Deerskin" Marks *to* HDI.
- §8 (confidentiality), §10.2 (no joint venture / co-ownership), plus full-text searches for "own", "intellectual property", "customer" — no ownership, assignment, work-product or data-title language anywhere.

**Why missing rather than deviation:** nothing assigns our IP or data to HDI (so not walk-away territory), but equally nothing vests ownership of the developed Site or the customer/transaction data in us, and there is no licence back for HDI-developed or HDI-embedded materials. Neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met, and there is no usable clause to redline — so the gap is filled rather than amended. Note that §10.2's "co-ownership" disclaimer addresses the corporate relationship, not IP title, so it does not cure the gap.

**Proposal (validated ok:true):** new §5.5 "Ownership" inserted after p0035 — we own the Site, Content, Marks and all customer/order/transaction data (with HDI assigning any interest it holds); HDI retains its pre-existing platform, tools and know-how and grants us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to embedded HDI materials; express no-joint-ownership and no-assignment-to-HDI language. This is the preferred position and preserves HDI's legitimate platform ownership, so it should be uncontroversial.
